author: human
request:
Bug report: opening /owners?page=0 — or any page value below 1 — renders the
error page instead of the owner list. Expected behavior: the owner listing
treats any page value below 1 as the first page and responds with the normal
listing (HTTP 200). Find the cause, fix it, and cover the fix with a test.

author: product-requirements-expert
title: Owner list shows the first page for a page number below one
summary: Opening the owner list with a page number of zero or below shows the first page of owners with a normal response, instead of the error page.
acceptance_criteria: given a page number of 0 and no last name, when the owner list is requested, then the response is HTTP 200 and renders the owner list, not the error page
given a negative page number and no last name, when the owner list is requested, then the response is HTTP 200 and renders the owner list, not the error page
given a page number below 1, when the owner list is requested, then the listing shows the same owners and the same current page as a request for page 1
non_goals: Non-numeric page values: the intake names only page values below 1; their current behavior is unchanged and left open
Page numbers beyond the last page: outside the quoted request; behavior unchanged
The veterinarian directory's paging: the intake names only the owner listing; not in this slice
notes: Grounding: intake line 1 quotes the owner: 'the owner listing treats any page value below 1 as the first page and responds with the normal listing (HTTP 200). Find the cause, fix it, and cover the fix with a test.' The PRD states this behaviorally as REQ-OWN-005; the HTTP 200 wording stays in the acceptance criteria here. Observed cause, for design triage: the listing turns its one-based page number into a zero-based page index by subtracting one, and the paging library rejects a negative index, which surfaces as the error page. The one test name is data-driven over 0 and a negative value. Open for the owner, not scoped here: the veterinarian directory computes its page index the same way and likely fails identically on page values below 1.

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: Covered by existing memory: system-design.md § Contracts, where the OwnerController row serves search with paging, plus security-principles.md § Trust Boundaries (external input: validate type, range, and shape before use). The one-based page request parameter is external input crossing the web boundary. Normalizing a value below 1 to the first page is range handling at that boundary, the request-binding duty that architecture-principles.md's Web controller row admits. It is not a business rule, so the checklist item barring new controller rules does not apply. Cause confirmed by grep on OwnerController.java (no IDE oracle connected, so this rests on the weaker basis): the private paging helper builds its page request from the one-based page minus one, and the paging library rejects a negative index. That exception reaches the error page. Fix shape: in the GET /owners handler, normalize the one-based page to at least 1 once, before anything reads it. Both the repository query and the currentPage model attribute then see the normalized value, which acceptance criterion 3 requires. No new type, package, dependency, or pattern. The only design-doc write is REQ-OWN-005 joining the OwnerController Contracts row.
integration_points: Repository boundary (OwnerRepository): the new test joins OwnerControllerTests, whose @WebMvcTest slice context already registers OwnerRepository as a @MockitoBean. A hand-written double would need its own test class and context, so the existing fixture's framework stub is the conscious exception (testing-principles.md § Mocking Policy: tolerated in the existing suite). Stub findByLastNameStartingWith for the empty last name with a multi-owner page, matching the Pageable on its page index being 0 (argThat on getPageNumber), not on a literal page size. A wrong index then falls through to the unstubbed default and the test fails.

Framework transport: MockMvc, the sanctioned web-test harness (CLAUDE.md § Testing Strategy). Assert HTTP 200, view owners/ownersList, and model attribute currentPage equal to 1, for page values 0 and a negative value in the one data-driven test theOwnerListShouldShowTheFirstPageForAPageNumberBelowOne.

Binding: no new entry point. The existing GET /owners handler keeps page as a request-scoped int request parameter. The Owner model attribute keeps its existing disallowed-identifier binder, and no persisted type is newly bound.

patterns.description: GET /owners handler: the one-based page enters here and feeds both the paging helper and the pagination model, so the normalization belongs here and nowhere downstream
Private paging helper converting the one-based page to a zero-based index; unchanged except that it now receives an already-normalized page

risks.risk: Clamping only the zero-based index inside the paging helper leaves currentPage at the raw value (0 or negative) in the model. The listing then does not match page 1, which breaches acceptance criterion 3, and the template's pagination links render from a bogus current page.
risks.mitigation: Normalize the one-based page once at the handler entry (security-principles.md § Trust Boundaries: validate at the boundary, and past the boundary internal code trusts its contracts); assert currentPage equals 1 in the test.

risks.risk: Subtracting one before clamping overflows at the int minimum. It wraps to a large positive index and yields an empty page and a not-found result instead of the first page.
risks.mitigation: Clamp the one-based page before the subtraction, never the index after it (security-principles.md § Trust Boundaries: range-check external input before use).

risks.risk: Scope creep into non-goals: non-numeric page values, pages beyond the last, and the veterinarian directory.
risks.mitigation: Leave the type-mismatch path and the vet controller untouched; the prd-entry non_goals bound the slice (architecture-principles.md § Design Validation Checklist: no rule added beyond the slice).

notes: Autofix audit: no design-doc-autofix records in the log; skipped. Five-signal foundational check: no signal trips (design doc confirmed in part, language/framework ADR present, vocabulary confirmed, no project-level concern touched, no new bounded context). For the owner, outside this slice: VetController.java:61 builds its page request the same way (one-based page minus one) and will fail identically for page values below 1. Durable memory does not record it; it needs its own intake, which would change the same line and add a REQ-VET id to the VetController Contracts row.

author: change-grader
summary: clamp owner-list page below one to the first page

blast_radius.note: One production file in one module: a single Math.max clamp at the GET /owners handler entry plus two call-site substitutions in OwnerController; the rest is one parameterized test and a one-row doc update each in prd.md and system-design.md, with no sensitive or security-surface paths.

semantic_surprise.note: Read the hunks against the full handler: Math.max(page, 1) runs before the page - 1 conversion in findPaginatedForOwnersLastName (OwnerController.java:141), both former uses of the raw page (the repository call and addPaginationModel) now take currentPage with no leftover raw read, and pages of 1 or above pass through unchanged, so the only behavior change is the intended one, including the Integer.MIN_VALUE overflow case.

test_adequacy.note: The parameterized test covers 0, -1 and Integer.MIN_VALUE, stubs the repository only for page index 0 (the setup stub is Franklin-only, so nothing masks a wrong index), and asserts HTTP 200, the list view, currentPage 1 and the returned owners; it would fail against the pre-fix code and against the tempting clamp-inside-the-helper alternative.
